rationale: The assistant correctly and immediately told the customer to stop using the microwave, stop resetting the trip, not open it, and get an engineer, with a sound high-voltage warning. However its only diagnostic question ('is it plugged into its own dedicated socket, or sharing with other high-power items like a kettle?') and the follow-up framing ('can easily overload standard extension leads') steer toward an overload explanation, when the whole-kitchen trip on Start plus a 'loud bang inside' points to an appliance earth-leakage/interlock fault; it never asked whether the trip persists with the microwave unplugged or tried another socket, nor mentioned the door. Safe and sensible overall, but the escalation lacked the useful diagnostic context (appliance-side fault, likely replace a cheap unit, electrician only if trips continue unplugged) that would have best served the homeowner.
